name: Torsional Filament Web Cassette TFW-2
description:
The TFW-2 is a dual-barrel cassette system for the TFP-6 'Garrote' torsional filament projector, containing 8 magnetically tipped anchor nodes connected by monofilament wire in a precisely coiled deployment package. Each cassette provides a single deployment — 4 anchor nodes from each barrel — that creates a web of high-tension monofilament across a 3-18 meter span. The anchor nodes magnetically attach to ferrous surfaces and the filament auto-tensions between them, creating an invisible barrier that lacerates anything that contacts it.

The monofilament wire is the cassette's active component — a carbon nanotube composite strand approximately 0.02mm in diameter, invisible to the naked eye under most lighting conditions and strong enough to maintain structural integrity under 400kg of tensile load. Under the torsional stress applied by the anchor nodes' rotary mechanisms, the filament develops a cutting edge that will sever soft tissue, light clothing, and thin metal on contact. The filament remains under tension for approximately 90 seconds before the anchor nodes' torsion springs exhaust, at which point the web goes slack and becomes merely a tripping hazard.

Reloading the TFP-6 requires replacing both cassettes — a process that takes approximately 45 seconds of careful handling, as the monofilament in a fresh cassette is under pre-tension that can lacerate the operator's hands if the cassette is mishandled. Experienced operators wear cut-resistant gloves during reload, and field reports document multiple hand injuries from improper cassette handling.
legality: Prohibited — classified as indiscriminate area-denial weapon
specifications:
anchor_nodes_per_deployment: 8 (4 per barrel)
filament_diameter: 0.02mm carbon nanotube composite
web_span: 3-18m adjustable
tension_duration: 90 seconds nominal, 60 seconds under load
tensile_strength: 400kg per strand
reload_time: ~45 seconds (both cassettes)
shelf_life: Indefinite (mechanical, no degradation)
variants: TFW-2 Extended (reinforced torsion springs, 180-second tension, heavier cassettes)
TFW-2 Conductive (electrified filament, adds electrical incapacitation to laceration, requires power cell)
TFW-2 Marker (UV-fluorescent filament, visible under UV illumination for forensic or training use)
cultural_context: The TFW-2 cassette and its parent weapon system occupy a particular niche in Meridian 88's assassination toolkit — a nearly invisible trap that can be deployed in seconds and removed (or self-removes) in minutes. The weapon's indiscriminate nature is both its strength and its moral burden: the monofilament web does not distinguish between the target and a bystander who walks through the same corridor. Among operators, the Garrote is treated with the kind of professional distance reserved for weapons that create collateral damage by design rather than by accident. The 45-second reload time also means that in a running engagement, the TFP-6 is effectively a single-shot weapon — one deployment, then you're done.
story_hooks: A pedestrian in a corporate district walked into an invisible monofilament web stretched across a service corridor — the injuries are consistent with TFW-2 deployment, but the anchor nodes were already retrieved, suggesting the trap was set for someone else and the pedestrian was collateral.

A modified TFW-2 cassette has been recovered with anchor nodes that embed in non-ferrous surfaces using adhesive rather than magnets — someone has expanded the Garrote's deployment options to include glass, concrete, and plastic surfaces.
